It's been a LONG time since I've updated my PC, and now with Doom released, I've got to get a new GPU. My current rig is an i7 (2600), 16gb of RAM, and a Radeon 5750 GPU. My PSU is only 460W and I don't think I can take a 12" long GPU in my case (current card is 7.25").

I really want to keep my purchase as far below $170 as I can push it so finding good sales is probably paramount. Right now it looks like the best I can hope to get is a GTX 960 (4gb) or an R9 389 (4gb).

The best deal I've found are $169 for the Gigabyte GeForce GTX 960 (at Amazon w/$20 MIR) Fry's had an R9 380 for $149 (after rebate) but they're sold out online and I don't live near a brick & mortar store. Craigslist has been a complete bust. Nobody is selling anything worth buying in my area. Ebay has been especially disappointing. I'm pretty much resigned to trying to find a good sale.

I know the GTX 950 has gotten similar benchmarks as the 960, but I'm not sure dropping to 2gb is the way to go given that I'm buying this card solely to play Doom. I'm happy to hear any recommendations, suggestions, or deals you might be aware of.

Recommendation: WAIT!

NVIDIA's new video cards (or maybe just the reference cards) will be out by the end of the month and AMD will be dropping their new series shortly after. And when new video cards come out, old video cards go on sale. That'll be your time to strike.

I'm not gonna recommend a specific model because budget is a factor, but I've got two recommendations. First, for your budget, stick to AMD. AMD is pure bang for your buck, and even though they've got a reputation for software headaches they've been doing some major overhauls to their drivers and the future is bright. I have an NVIDIA card and my SO has a newer AMD card, and I've been impressed with the price/performance with new software. I'll probably end up buying AMD next year. Second, make sure you get 4GB VRAM. No exceptions. Save however much you need to make sure you get it, but it's crucial if you're a person who goes a long time between video card upgrades. Textures are just getting bigger and beefier, and 2GB VRAM is already starting to get a bit limiting with great game mods and newer, huge games like ARK.

I know the 1080 and 1070 will be getting released very soon, but those are the very high-end of their line (and far outside my budget). I'm sure that will impact the price of their high-end cards, but given the current retail on those, I doubt they'll fall within my budget. Do you think stuff like the GTX 960 or R9 380 will be immediately impacted by the release of the 1080/70?

I wouldn't mind waiting if I thought a price drop (on cards in my budget) was imminent, but there hasn't been any talk of new cards in the tier I'm shooting for (at least I haven't read anything). Most of the cards I'm looking at look like they were released in early Fall of 2015 so it wouldn't surprise me if it wasn't until August before new stuff in that tier got released. Ugh. I played this upgrade game back in the 90s because of id Software games, and now I'm having to do it again to play this new version of Doom! :)

New video cards tend to usher sales and price drops on older cards, even if it was just the last generation. The newer, the lower the price drop, but all of them tend to see a sale. It's not about new cards coming out in your price tier, its about new cards that need to fill warehouses and store shelves meaning that older product needs to be moved ASAP!

The only thing you lose by waiting is time not spent playing DOOM. You might scope a good deal before new card releases, maybe people trying to Craigslist their cards to upgrade, maybe just a good Newegg deal, whatever! The temptation of DOOM is strong, I know. Been trying to keep myself from buying it because I know it'll be half off in a year and I can be patient. A few months is nothing to wait for video card deals when it'll be the card you'll using for years on end, though.
